title: add benchmark-lab workload runners, profiling baselines, and reporting pipeline v53
author: Aisha Khatri
description: This PR adds a new set of representative workload runners, updated profiling baselines, and a reporting pipeline for the Benchmark Lab (v53). Motivation: recent runtime changes (kernel selection and batching heuristics) require updated baseline measurements across representative workloads so we can detect regressions and guide optimization. The main pieces are: 1) new workload runners that emulate multi-tenant mixed workloads (conversational + streaming + embedding), including parameterized client-side pacing and KV-cache warmup sequences; 2) profiling baselines (v53) covering cold-start, warm-start, and KV-cache heavy scenarios; 3) a reporting DAG that ingests runner outputs, computes summary metrics (p50/p95 token latency, tail GPU utilization, per-request cost), and publishes HTML/CSV artifacts; 4) CI job that schedules periodic runs and stores artifacts in the benchmark GCS bucket. Checklist: - [x] Add representative runners and configs - [x] Add profiling baseline YAMLs + sample outputs - [x] Add reporting pipeline DAG + templates - [x] Update CI to schedule nightly runs - [x] Docs: README and runbook updated - [x] Add unit/integration tests and simple smoke perf checks See linear ENG-2378 for the workplan and artifact retention policy. Related PRs: #142010 (v52 reporting), #134567 (profiling infra). This description contains the full motivation, testing notes, and migration instructions: to roll out, release the pipeline in staging and run 3 nightly iterations to seed the baselines; the reporting job will automatically tag the run as "v53" and compare against the previous stable baselines. Backwards compatibility: runners are additive and do not change existing v5x baselines. Contact: @aisha for any questions.
commits: Create mixed-workload runner and parameterized CLI (aisha/bench-runners)
Add profiling baselines v53 and example outputs
Add reporting pipeline DAG and publish templates
Update CI to add nightly benchmark-lab workflow and retention settings
files_patch_snippets: benchmark-lab/runners/mixed_workloads.py: def run_workload(args):\n    # simplified: dispatch mixed conversation + embedding + streaming\n    ...

benchmark-lab/profiling/baselines/v53.yaml: baseline_sets:
  - name: cold_start
    description: 'Cold start with empty cache'
    metrics: [p50_latency, p95_latency, gpu_util]

benchmark-lab/reporting/pipeline_v53.yaml: tasks:
  - name: ingest
  - name: aggregate
  - name: publish_html

Aisha Khatri: Added 'generator_version' to baselines and bumped test vectors. Responded with an explanation of expected drift and how we will handle rebaselining.
Oscar Reed: Approved after verifying that the reporting DAG has circuit-breaker timeouts for long-running aggregations.
release_notes: Adds v53 benchmark-lab representative workload runners, profiling baselines, and a reporting pipeline. Nightly CI job created to seed baselines and publish reports. See docs/benchmark-lab/README.md for usage.
notes: This change is additive; no runtime config changes required for existing baselines. Staging runs are required to populate v53 baselines before relying on alerts.
